If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overconfidence bias.  
If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to compensate for bearish momentum.  
If sentiment swings sharply (±0.33) in the last 3 days, apply a 2–3% downward correction to late horizon (16–30 days) to dampen volatility overhang.  
When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and history shows a recent peak, reduce forecast by 1–2% for mid horizon to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is positive but forecasted price is above 75.00, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon to avoid inflationary overestimation.  
If sentiment is negative and forecasted price is below 70.00, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon to counteract pessimism-induced underestimation.
